page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v6 is a compute-focused instance variant within the general-purpose D-series lineage, configured with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside integrated high-speed local disk storage. The instance operates on the x86_64 architecture and is driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Resource provisioning provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX.

System memory totals 32.0 GB, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture combines support for remote premium storage with a bundled local NVMe SSD capacity of 944 GB for scratch space and swap. There are no discrete graphics processing units attached. Network throughput supports static web serving transfers up to 28.78 GB/sec, while hypervisor virtualization is controlled via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core efficiency, with Geekbench single-core recording 2163.0 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 31.37 GB/sec, placing both in the top 25 percent. In multi-core operations, the instance registered a Geekbench multi-core score of 13256.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 26706.63. Under CPU-driven machine learning tests utilizing small 135M parameter models, text generation reached 396.44 tokens per second, ranking in the top decile. In-memory database workloads reached 22.76 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

The constrained 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio presents a tradeoff for memory-dense datasets, but improves resource cost efficiency for compute-heavy processes that do not consume large pools of memory. Microsoft Azure D16lds_v6 is structured for web application backends, batch transformation, code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, and compute-oriented workloads requiring high-speed local scratch storage.

It is provisioned with a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio providing 32.0 GB of RAM alongside 944 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, while omitting discrete GPUs. Benchmarks exhibit competitive single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 2163.0, strong gzip compression at 31.37 GB/sec, and top-tier CPU-driven small model token generation at 396.44 tokens per second. The balanced high clock speed and local NVMe storage make it effective for compilation tasks, batch data manipulation, web application hosting, and CI/CD pipelines.
